public_rationale: Billions of infrastructure spending are documented. The reported Chinese AI-stock collapse is a serious candidate event and cannot be ignored. Its geography and the lack of matching evidence of a broad investment collapse prevent it from settling the wider Rot-Com prediction. Continued spending also cannot disprove an inevitable future collapse. The compound forecast remains open.
limitations: A China-only interpretation could change the assessment of the collapse clause, but the post describes a broader technology system.
The spending evidence covers one company and includes non-AI assets.
The accessible market evidence does not establish all dimensions of the proposed early-resolution rule.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The tech growth bubble, including AI, will inevitably pop, with billions invested in hardware and software until it does.

statement.excerpt: The Rot-Com bubble will inevitably pop, but until it does, billions will be plowed into building hardware and software to inflate the Rot-Com bubble in the hopes that the growth-at-all-costs party will never end.

from_speaker: The Rot-Com bubble will inevitably pop
billions will be plowed into building hardware and software
our_interpretation: The context describes a broad technology growth and investment bubble, including AI and major technology companies.
A pop means a sharp, sustained collapse in valuations and investment across that sector, not an isolated company failure or regional correction.
The spending clause predicts aggregate investment before the collapse. It supplies no company-specific accounting metric; metric_scope is therefore null.
The forecast supplies no deadline, numerical collapse threshold or minimum duration. No such threshold is invented here.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes a broad, sharp and sustained technology valuation and investment collapse, with billions invested in hardware and software beforehand.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive event makes the predicted collapse impossible. Continued growth, continued investment or recovery from one correction cannot disprove an eventual collapse without a deadline.

evidence.explanation: The disclosure documents billions of realized infrastructure investment, including AI and non-AI assets. One company's expenditure neither measures the whole claimed bubble nor establishes a collapse.

Citing Reuters, the article reports a 40% four-month STAR50 decline and substantial losses among Chinese hardware companies. This is material evidence of a regional collapse, but does not establish a sustained sector-wide collapse in both valuations and investment.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable records showing a sharp, persistent collapse across major technology valuations, financing and investment, together with documented pre-collapse hardware and software spending.
